thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: service-discovery error rate spike in az-c1 — SRV resolution failures reported for consul-backed services, error rate ~22% over 5m. Paging oncall: @maria (pager). Links: https://console.incidents/2321001234 and runbook: https://playbooks/redwood/dns-service-resolve.md :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): On it. Giving initial context: seen sudden jump in SRV NXDOMAIN / timeout from kiosk and batch workers. Which clusters?

jordan (sre): seen notably from eu-west and us-west clusters hitting services in az-c1. Traceroutes show asymmetric path after last peering change. Suspect ECMP/BGP split.

incident-bot: Related alerts: coreDNS-5xx-count, consul-query-latency, netegress-bgp-flap. Auto-escalation in 10m if no ack.

maria (oncall): quick checks: digging consul SRV from a few pods.
```bash
# from app pod in eu-west
dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.prod.svc.cluster.local @10.3.0.12
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short SRV _api._tcp.service.prod.svc.cluster.local @10.3.0.12
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

maria (oncall): also pulling coredns logs for az-c1: increased EOFs and i/o timeouts.

jordan (sre): traceroute from eu-west pod to az-c1 coredns vip
```
traceroute to 10.3.0.12 (10.3.0.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.5.1.1  0.5 ms  0.6 ms  0.7 ms
 2  100.64.0.45  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.2  45.2 ms  44.9 ms  44.8 ms
 5  203.0.113.14  46.1 ms  45.9 ms  46.0 ms
 6  10.3.0.12  46.4 ms !H  46.5 ms !H  46.6 ms !H
```
jordan (sre): !H hints host unreachable intermittently from one ECMP path. Matches BGP churn window we saw at 2321001200.

gaurav (neteng): confirmed there was a maintenance blast to peer fabric in az-c1 at 2321001180 that toggled a subset of egress ECMP peers. Some routes flapped and caused transient asymmetric forwarding; control-plane withdrew a handful of /24s for ~90s. We're seeing packet drops to the local DNS VIPs on one path.

samantha (support): customers reporting intermittent 502s for service-to-service calls; batch jobs retrying and backoff increasing costs. Major customer A reported degraded health checks. Ticket numbers: TKT-4451, TKT-4452.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) failover DNS traffic away from az-c1 egress path by adjusting route policy to prefer az-b peers, 2) scale coredns in az-c1 to absorb retries, 3) bump consul agent query retry and lower circuit-breaker threshold for 10m, 4) inform customers. I'll run steps 1+2 now.

maria (oncall): applying route policy (temp):
```bash
redwood-netctl policy apply --prefix 10.3.0.0/22 --prefer-peer az-b --reason "emergency: az-c1 dns path drop"
# confirmed new BGP attr set, propagating
```

devops-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: route-policy applied. Wait 30s and verify telemetry.

jordan (sre): scaling coredns in az-c1: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy coredns --replicas=6 --context=az-c1`

maria (oncall): increased replicas. Monitoring logs for errors.

maria (oncall): quick post-change dig:
```bash
# from eu-west pod after route change
dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.prod.svc.cluster.local @10.3.0.12
0 10 644 10.3.0.24
```
maria (oncall): SRV resolving now for some hosts. Error rate dropped to ~6% in last 2m.

gaura (neteng): I'm keeping a BGP watch. We'll re-enable the original ECMP peers only after we see stable route convergence for 30m.

samantha (support): updating customer A: "We have routed DNS traffic to alternate egress to mitigate packet loss. Expect reduced errors; our teams are monitoring. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

jordan (sre): other mitigation: increase consul client-side timeouts and add one extra retry to reduce visible downstream errors:
```hcl
consul_client_config {
  retries = 3
  request_timeout = "6s"
}
```
applied to rolling agents in az-c1.

maria (oncall): handoff note: I'm handing to @jordan (sre) for the next 30m while I rotate for breakfast. Handoff checklist: route-policy active, coredns replicas = 6, consul client retries = 3, watch netegress BGP. I'll be reachable by DM.

jordan (sre): ACK. I'll keep the channel updated. Current severity: Sev2 (widespread but mitigated). Will collect pcap from affected coredns nodes and start a timeline for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident update logged: severity=2, start=2321001234, mitigation=route-policy-failover, owner=jordan (sre). Pager will escalate to oncall manager in 40m if not resolved.

samantha (support): customers informed, support queue triaged; will gather customer impact summary for incident report.

maria (oncall): leaving handover note in ops ticket: "temporary route preference to az-b. Revert only when neteng confirms stable ECMP and we've validated 30m of clean SRV resolve telemetry."

jordan (sre): follow-ups: capture coredns heap/threads, collect consul latency histograms, correlate BGP logs. Postmortem owner: neteng + runtime infra.

devops-bot: NEXT STEPS: create incident doc at https://incidents/docs/2321001234, set postmortem template, assign owners.

jordan (sre): closing interim mitigation: continue monitoring. Will update with resolution or escalation. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
